extracted.intended_audience: short-story writers, editors, anthologists, and students of short fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection criteria used in a yearbook/critical summary for choosing the 'Roll of Honor' and 'Best Books' of short stories (American and foreign), plus evaluative comments on anthologies and individual volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roll of Honor selection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Only stories by American authors are listed. The best stories are indicated by an asterisk before the title. The index figures 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 prefixed to the name of the author indicate that his work has been included in the Rolls of Honor for 1914, 1915, 1916, 1917, 1918, 1919, and 1920 respectively. The list excludes reprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nationality (American) as an inclusion filter; mark exceptional pieces with an asterisk; record prior-year inclusions with prefixed index figures; do not include reprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / formal innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Works that 'moulded a new form for these stories which disobeys successfully all the codes of story writing' are highly valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovation and the successful breaking of conventional 'codes of story writing' is a criterion for high distinction (example: Bercovici's volume praised for moulding a new form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance / emergence of new voices
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The essential point is that he and Sherwood Anderson are the most significant new short story writers who have emerged in America within the past five years.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a volume or author for their significance to the field (does it mark an important new voice or movement?). Emerging importance is a factor in 'best' judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical craftsmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical competence is a recognized quality: a book may be 'a piece of extremely competent craftsmanship' whose interest to the man of letters is 'largely technical.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate structural, technical, and craft merits even when overall literary value may be moderate; technically accomplished stories may be recommended for anthologies or study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic suspense and literary honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories containing 'dramatic suspense and a certain literary honesty' are singled out as excellent and recommendable to anthologists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for narrative tension (dramatic suspense) and perceived sincerity or 'honesty' in treatment as markers of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional fidelity and quiet humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualities such as 'homely fidelity and quiet humor' (in regional writing) make a collection 'distinctly worth reading.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faithful regional depiction and understated humor are positive qualities when assessing regional or localist short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value for students / pedagogical worth
rubrics_metrics.description: Anthologies that 'contain a number of standard texts' and are 'worthy of purchase by students of the short story' are considered valuable even if casually edited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider inclusion of canonical/standard texts and overall usefulness as a teaching or reference collection when judging anthologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection quality (conventional vs. adventurous selections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selections that are 'of a thoroughly conventional nature' are criticized; conversely, anthologies that 'introduce a number of good stories which are likely to prove new to most readers' are praised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate editors on whether they merely reprint conventional/expected texts or whether they surface less-known but valuable material; adventurous, instructive selection is preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation and editorial apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: An editor who 'has added to the value of the volume by elaborate annotation' increases the anthology's worth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly or informative annotation that clarifies context and meaning is a positive factor in assessing anthologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of sequels / freshness of material
rubrics_metrics.description: 'It is a wise counsel of perfection which says that sequels are barred,' and attempting to repeat a prior artistic success (a sequel) is viewed skeptically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor fresh, original material rather than sequels; repetition of an earlier thematic field or formula is likely to reduce critical esteem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted range as a virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer who 'has voluntarily restricted her range, but she has simply "curtailed her circumference to enlarge her liberty," and I believe this volume is likely to outlast many books which are more widely talked about.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A focused/restricted thematic or stylistic range can enhance artistic freedom and longevity; depth over breadth can be a criterion of lasting value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical innovation merits study even without high literary value
rubrics_metrics.description: Volumes that 'have solved some important new technical problems' may 'repay attentive study' and have pedagogical value even if they 'possess no special literary value.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and recommend works for their technical innovations to students and practitioners, separate from their broader literary worth.
